title: Causal order of single-cell readings on a contract chain

key_results.statement: Outcome-averaged influence: $\Delta_t=P_j(t\mid R_i)-P_j(t)=\langle\Psi_1\vert\mathcal M_i(Q_t)-Q_t\vert\Psi_1\rangle$ with $Q_t=e^{\mathrm iC\delta}\Pi'_te^{-\mathrm iC\delta}$ and $\mathcal M_i(X)=\sum_s\Pi_sX\Pi_s$; $\delta P=\sum_t\lvert\Delta_t\rvert$.
No influence without delay: $P_j(\cdot\mid R_i)=P_j(\cdot)$ whenever $\lambda_2\le\lambda_1$, for all cells, starts and readings.

Locality: $[\mathrm{ad}_C^k\Pi'_t,\Pi_s]=0$ for $k<r$ and $[\mathrm{ad}_C^r\Pi'_t,\Pi_s]=[K_t,\Pi_s]$ with $K_t=\mathrm{ad}_{J_{i-1}}\cdots\mathrm{ad}_{J_j}\Pi'_t$ ($i>j$), independent of the $D_m$ and of the booking.

Leading order: $\Delta_t=\Gamma_t\delta^r+O(\delta^{r+1})$ with $\Gamma_t=\frac{1}{r!}\operatorname{Tr}[(\mathcal M_i(V)-V)\,\mathrm i^rK_t]$, $V$ the view of the cells from $j$ to $i$ at $\lambda_1$.
$\delta P=\delta^r\sum_t\lvert\Gamma_t\rvert+O(\delta^{r+1})$: the lowest possible power of the delay is $\delta^r$, $r=\lvert i-j\rvert$.
Qubit chain $J_1=g\sigma^x_1\sigma^x_2$, $J_m=g\sigma^z_m\sigma^x_{m+1}$ ($2\le m\le r$), arbitrary $D_m$, place readings on cells $1$ and $r+1$.
For the chain (7.6) and start $\lvert+\rangle\otimes\lvert{+\mathrm i}\rangle^{\otimes r}$: $\Gamma_0=-\Gamma_1=-2^{r-1}g^r/r!$ and $\delta P=(2g\delta)^r/r!+O(\delta^{r+1})$ for every $r\ge1$.
Exact case $n=2$, $D=0$, $J_1=g\sigma^x_1\sigma^x_2$, start $\lvert+\rangle\lvert{+\mathrm i}\rangle$: $\delta P=\lvert\sin(2g\delta)\rvert$.

Chain Lieb-Robinson bound: $\lVert[A(\delta),B]\rVert\le2\lVert A\rVert\lVert B\rVert\sum_{k\ge r}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^k/k!$ for $A$, $B$ on cells at distance $r\ge1$, uniform in $n$ and independent of the $D_i$.

$\delta P\le2(1-\tfrac1m)\sum_{k\ge r}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^k/k!\le2\sum_{k\ge r}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^k/k!\le\frac{2(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^r}{r!}e^{2\lVert J\rVert\delta}$ for every start, every pair of readings ($m$ classes of $R_i$) and every $\delta\ge0$; only the first form is attained at leading order, for $m=2$.
If $\delta P=0$ on an interval $(0,\varepsilon)$ then $\delta P=0$ for all $\delta\ge0$: no delayed onset of the influence.
The set $\mathcal I_{ij}$ of delays with influence is either empty or $(0,\infty)\setminus E_{ij}$ with $E_{ij}$ discrete and empty near $0$: there is no sharp cone.

Region of guaranteed small influence: $\mathcal S_\epsilon=\{(r,\delta):2\sum_{k\ge r}(2\lVert J\rVert\delta)^k/k!<\epsilon\}=\{0\le\delta<\delta_\epsilon(r)\}$; for $\lVert J\rVert=0$ it is the whole domain.
Inner cone: $\delta P\le\frac{2}{1-2\lVert J\rVert/v}(2e\lVert J\rVert/v)^r$ for $0\le\delta\le r/v$ and $v>2e\lVert J\rVert$.

For $\lVert J\rVert>0$ the boundary of $\mathcal S_\epsilon$ moves at $\lim_{r\to\infty}r/\delta_\epsilon(r)=v_{\rm LR}=2e\lVert J\rVert$ cells per unit $\lambda$, independent of $\epsilon$, $n$ and the $D_i$.
$(i,\lambda_1)\prec(j,\lambda_2)$ if some reading at $(i,\lambda_1)$ influences some reading at $(j,\lambda_2)$ for some start.
$e_1\prec e_2$ implies $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$.
Fixed-delay statement: for fixed cells $i,j$ and fixed $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$, $e_1\prec e_2$ for all contract terms outside a closed null set that depends on the delay.
Non-transitivity: for $n=2$, $D=0$, $J_1=g\sigma^x_1\sigma^x_2$, $(1,0)\prec(2,\tfrac{\pi}{4g})\prec(1,\tfrac{\pi}{2g})$ but $(1,0)\nprec(1,\tfrac{\pi}{2g})$.

Exceptional chains: $\mathcal X_{ij}=\{C:[U_\delta^\dagger\mathcal D_jU_\delta,\mathcal D_i]=0$ for some $\delta>0\}$ and $\mathcal X=\bigcup_{i,j}\mathcal X_{ij}$; $C\notin\mathcal X$ if and only if $\prec$ is the order of $\lambda$.
Blind delays: $\Lambda^{ij}_C=\{\delta>0:[U_\delta^\dagger\mathcal O_jU_\delta,\mathcal O_i]=0\}$, and $\mathcal X^{\rm bl}_{ij}=\{C:\Lambda^{ij}_C\neq\emptyset\}$.

For $i\neq j$ and every $n\ge2$, the chains having an exceptional delay for $(i,j)$ that is not blind form a null set: generically, a positive delay without influence between different cells is a blind delay.
For $n=2$, $\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal X)=0$: for almost every $C$, $e_1\prec e_2\iff\lambda_1<\lambda_2$ for all events; for $n\ge3$ the same question is undecided (blind delays, same-cell pairs).

definitions.name: Outcome-averaged influence of R_i on outcome t of R_j
Dephasing map of the reading R_i
Nested commutator of the links between the two cells
Set of delays with influence from cell i to cell j, and its discrete complement
Region of guaranteed small influence and its boundary
Speed of the boundary of the small-influence region
Blind delays and chains with a blind delay

open_issues: U1 (n ≥ 3, different cells): not decided whether a generic chain has no blind delay, i.e. whether the set of chains with a blind delay (7.23) is null; if it is, (7.24) makes the exceptional set for different cells null.

U2 (n ≥ 3, same cell): not decided whether the chains with an exceptional delay for two readings on the same cell form a null set; if U1 and U2 hold, (7.25) extends to every n and ≺ is generically the order of λ and transitive.
v_LR = 2e‖J‖ is the speed of the bound's ε-boundary; the actual front speed of a given chain may be lower and is not determined; attainment of the bound is shown only at leading order, for m = 2.

Out of scope: events defined by records, sequences of more than two readings, other contract graphs, the relation to the maximal speed of 03-ilang-space, and whether the order of λ is detectable (criterion 8).

consistency_checks.check: Cut link (J_m = 0 between the two cells): δP ≡ 0 exactly, in agreement with K_t = 0, with the recursion behind (7.11), with an empty delay set in (7.14), and with every delay being blind as (7.24) requires.

n = 2 exact solution δP = |sin 2gδ|: leading term 2gδ agrees with (7.7), the m = 2 bound e^{2gδ} − 1 holds, zeros are isolated, and the exceptional delay π/(2g) is blind for a chain that violates (G), inside the null set allowed by (7.25).
Limit δ → 0 and dimensions: δP → 0 continuously with (7.2), Σ_t Γ_t = 0, ‖J‖δ is dimensionless and v_LR has the dimension of ‖J‖ (cells per unit λ).
